title: Can we have meaning without God?
where: Four live events in Vancouver, Dublin and London, moderated by Bret Weinstein and Douglas Murray
question: Can reason and science alone give us morality and meaning, or do we need religion's stories?
sides: Sam Harris

Morality is about the wellbeing of conscious creatures, and we can study that with reason and science. Religious dogma causes real harm, and the genuine insights of spiritual life, such as the loss of the sense of self in meditation, are available without believing anything on faith.
Jordan Peterson

The Bible and other religious stories encode wisdom refined over thousands of years about how to live and confront chaos. Western values rest on a Judeo-Christian foundation, and a purely rational framework cannot carry meaning or motivate people the way those stories do.
agree: Truth matters, suffering is real, totalitarian ideologies must be resisted, and something like spiritual experience is profoundly important.
listen: Their first conversation, on Harris's podcast in 2017, stalled for two hours over what the word 'truth' even means. Listen for how that disagreement keeps returning: scientific truth versus truth as what helps us live.

live.title: What gives your life meaning?
live.text: Write down three things that give your life meaning. Each day this week, ask of one: could I defend this without God? With God?

title: Has science buried God?
where: The God Delusion Debate, University of Alabama at Birmingham, 3 October 2007
question: Does science make belief in God unnecessary, or even irrational?
sides: Richard Dawkins

Evolution by natural selection explains the appearance of design in living things. Invoking God explains nothing, because a designer would need explaining too, and is far more improbable than what it is meant to explain.
John Lennox

Science explains how things work, not why there is anything at all. Science itself depends on the universe being rationally intelligible, which fits a creator. Explaining an engine by physics doesn't rule out Henry Ford.
agree: Science is a great human achievement, evidence matters, and faith should not mean believing things without reasons.
listen: Listen for Lennox's Henry Ford analogy about different levels of explanation, and Dawkins's question 'who designed the designer?'

live.title: One level deeper
live.text: Each day this week, ask "why?" one level deeper than usual about something you take for granted.

title: Is religion a force for good?
question: Be it resolved: religion is a force for good in the world.
sides: Christopher Hitchens
Religion poisons everything: it claims authority it does not have, divides people, and blesses cruelty. Whatever good believers do, they could do without it.
Tony Blair
Faith motivates enormous good, from hospitals to the fight against malaria. Religion can be abused like anything powerful, but the answer is open-minded faith, not no faith.
agree: Both condemned religious extremism and violence, and treated each other with notable warmth.
listen: Hitchens was already seriously ill with cancer at the time. Notice the friendship between two men who disagreed about everything that matters most.
search: Munk Debate Hitchens Blair religion force for good

live.title: See faith at work
live.text: This week, visit a place where people of faith serve others, such as a food bank or night shelter. Help if you can, and notice what you see.

title: Does morality need God?
question: Is the foundation of morality natural or supernatural?
sides: William Lane Craig

If God does not exist, objective moral values and duties do not exist either; they would just be the by-products of evolution. Because we know some things really are evil, God is the best explanation of morality.
Sam Harris
Morality concerns the wellbeing of conscious creatures. The worst possible misery for everyone is bad by any meaningful definition, so we can build a science of morality without God.
agree: Some things are objectively right and wrong, and moral relativism is a mistake.
listen: Listen for Harris's thought experiment of 'the worst possible misery for everyone', and Craig's reply that Harris has redefined 'good' rather than grounded it.
search: William Lane Craig Sam Harris debate Notre Dame 2011

live.title: Notice what is truly wrong
live.text: Each time this week you feel that something is truly wrong, write it down. At the end of the week, ask what makes it wrong.

title: What is a human being?
where: Sheldonian Theatre, Oxford, 23 February 2012, chaired by the philosopher Anthony Kenny
question: The nature of human beings and the question of their ultimate origin.
sides: Richard Dawkins
Humans are products of evolution like every other living thing. Consciousness and morality are remarkable, but they need no supernatural explanation.
Rowan Williams
Evolution is not in doubt, but a human being is more than a mechanism: we are capable of relationship, self-giving love and openness to truth, which point beyond ourselves to God.
agree: Evolution is true, and the Genesis stories are not a science textbook.
listen: This was a conversation more than a debate, between a scientist and the then Archbishop of Canterbury. Notice how differently they use the word 'explanation'.

live.title: Be fully present
live.text: Spend ten minutes each day this week with one person, phones away. Notice what a human being is.

title: Is there any good evidence for God?
where: "Does God Exist?", Biola University, La Mirada, California, 4 April 2009, moderated by the broadcaster Hugh Hewitt
question: Does God exist, and who has to prove what?
sides: William Lane Craig

Five lines of evidence point the same way. The universe began to exist, so it needs a cause beyond space and time. Its physical constants are finely tuned for life. Objective moral values need a foundation beyond us. The best explanation of the empty tomb, the appearances and the first disciples' sudden belief is that Jesus rose. And many people know God directly, in experience, as surely as they know other people.
Christopher Hitchens

The burden of proof lies with the one making the claim, and extraordinary claims need extraordinary evidence. A universe full of waste, extinction and cruelty does not look designed, and a believer can fit any discovery into the story after the event, which makes it impossible to test. Humans have been around for vast ages before the revelation believers describe, and people are moral through empathy and instinct, not divine command.
agree: Both said some things really are right and wrong, both accepted evolution and saw no conflict between it and the question of God as such, and neither claimed absolute certainty.
listen: Listen for the opening clash over who carries the burden of proof, Hitchens's question about why God waited so long before acting in history, and Craig's reply that the timing fitted the world in which the message could spread. Notice where each man answers the other, and where they talk past each other.

live.title: What would change your mind?
live.text: Each evening this week, write one line: what would make you more sure about God, and what would make you less sure? On the last day, read your lines back and ask whether you are holding both sides to the same standard.
